papers_read.title_as_printed: Spatio-temporal convolution for classification of alzheimer disease and mild cognitive impairment (Turhan, Kucuk, Ozturk Isik; Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine 221 (2022) 106825)

Multiscale convolution-attention model for efficient Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment diagnosis approach using sMRI (Khatri, Kim, Kwon; Applied Soft Computing 184 (2025) 113693) - BrainViT, matching the 2026-09-15 repoint

what_each_reports.P-30: (2+1)D CNN, whole-brain T1 MRI at 32x32x32, ADNI, binary AD vs MCI (507 scans/223 AD, 507 scans/204 MCI), 5-fold CV: AUC 0.85 +/- 0.046, validation accuracy 0.78 +/- 0.032.
what_each_reports.P-109: BrainViT hybrid CNN-transformer on 2D slices (about 50 axial/coronal/sagittal slices per subject, 54,300 slices) from 1075 ADNI subjects (390 AD, 370 MCI, 315 HC), images shuffled randomly and split 90/10: three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy 96.81%, AUC 98.05 (BrainViT-L). Binary results are reported only for AD/HC (97.13%, AUC 98.52) and MCI/HC (94.23%, AUC 97.15); no binary AD vs MCI result.

quantity_a: Cross-validated ROC-AUC for binary AD vs MCI discrimination, ADNI, whole-brain structural MRI (subject-level split).
quantity_b: Held-out accuracy for three-class AD vs MCI vs HC classification, ADNI, 2D sMRI slices with a random slice-level split.
incompatible_if_same: Cannot be assessed: P-109 reports no binary AD vs MCI figure, and a three-class accuracy is not an estimate of a binary AUC. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: binary AD vs MCI (P-30, registry T2) vs three-class AD/MCI/HC (P-109, registry T3). The record's 'T1' for both and 'task_equal: Yes' are wrong.
gates.validation_tier: match in tier (internal only), but P-109's split is over shuffled 2D slices from the same subjects, a leakage-prone design P-30 does not share.
gates.modality_family: match: structural T1 MRI in both.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different classification problem (binary vs three-class) and metric type (ROC-AUC vs accuracy).
performance_validity: flag plausibly applies to P-109 though the automatic test was not tripped: its 96.81% is just under 0.97, but its three-class AUC 98.05 and AD/HC accuracy 97.13% are at or above 0.97 on internal validation only, with no external cohort and a random slice-level split. The verdict does not rest on this.
independence: Distinct studies and author groups; both sample ADNI.
grounds: P-30's 0.85 is a binary AD-vs-MCI ROC-AUC; P-109's 96.81% is a three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy, so task and metric type both differ.
P-109 reports no binary AD-vs-MCI result that could be set against P-30.

P-109's evaluation shuffles 2D slices from the same subjects into train and test, a different validation design from P-30's cross-validation, and its near-ceiling internal figures would in any case bar it from a performance conflict.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-30: AUC ~0.85 on T1': P-30 is AD vs MCI (registry T2), not T1.
claim_b 'P-109: 96.81% Acc on T1': the figure is a three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy (registry T3).
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-109 binary AD-vs-MCI AUC from a subject-level split with an external cohort that excluded P-30's 0.85, on the same input representation; nothing of the kind is in P-109.
